note: The continuation message size is decoded directly from the attacker-controlled file bytes with no validation. A crafted file can set this to 0, 1, 2, or 3 bytes.
The unvalidated continuation message size is stored into the continuation message info structure for later processing.
The attacker-controlled continuation message size is copied into the chunk cache user data, which will be used as the read length for the continuation chunk.
The cache entry load size is set to the attacker-controlled continuation message size (0-3 bytes). No minimum size check is performed in release builds.
The metadata cache uses the attacker-controlled size as the buffer length. The HDassert(len > 0) is compiled out in release builds, so len can be 0-3.
A small heap buffer is allocated for the metadata image (len + extra space, where len is 0-3).
The small number of bytes (0-3) is read from the file into the small heap buffer. The read succeeds because the file contains data at that address.
The verify_chksum callback is invoked with actual_len equal to the attacker-controlled small size (0-3).
H5F_get_checksums is called with len=0-3. Inside, buf_size - H5_SIZEOF_CHKSUM underflows to a huge size_t value, causing a 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow READ past the end of the small heap buffer.
buf_size - 4 underflows when buf_size < 4, causing an out-of-bounds read of 4 bytes from the heap buffer, which is the heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 reported by ASan.
